A0095.title: Smart Contract Security Audit
A0095.definition: A systematic manual review and professional analysis of smart contract code to identify potential security vulnerabilities and logical flaws.
A0095.description: Smart contract security audit involves systematic manual review and rule matching of contract code by a professional team, applying judgment logic such as permission verification, reentrancy detection, integer overflow comparison, and sequence validation to identify security vulnerabilities and logical flaws. The audit report classifies findings by severity—critical, high, medium, and low—and provides remediation recommendations.
A0095.limitation: Manual audits depend on reviewer expertise. Attackers can bypass the audited scope through code obfuscation, cross-contract calls, or post-deployment upgrades, and complex logic flaws may remain false negatives. Audits cover only a specific version, are costly and slow, and can create false assurance when conclusions are overstated.

references.title: Smart Contract Vulnerabilities and Mitigation Strategies

A0095-001.title: Smart Contract Code Auditing and Public Verification
A0095-001.definition: Conduct third-party code audits before project launch and publicly verify the contract source code on blockchain explorers.
A0095-001.description: Reduce rug pull risks through transparency and professional review. Implementation points: Engage reputable auditing firms (e.g., CertiK, Quantstamp) to perform comprehensive code audits and publicly release audit reports; verify and publish contract source code on blockchain explorers such as Etherscan, allowing investors to inspect it; focus on checking for hidden mint functions, transaction pause functions, owner privileges, liquidity withdrawal backdoors, and other common rug pull techniques; examine upgrade permissions of proxy contracts to ensure they cannot be maliciously replaced; audited code should not be modified thereafter, and if modifications are required, a re-audit is necessary. Platforms like Coinbase recommend that investors prioritize projects that have undergone auditing.
A0095-001.limitation: Audits cannot guarantee discovery of every vulnerability. Attackers can bypass the published and verified code scope through proxy upgrades, unaudited components, or social engineering. Reports may also be forged or quoted out of context, causing users to misjudge safety, and an open-source audited project can still conduct a rug pull.
keywords: Smart Contract Code Auditing and Public Verification
